request: Build a demo of Tellurion: dummy data an audience can read cold, plus an animation of the orrery being created as the plan runs, touring the spine and the key. Highlight the Features Ledger (with Broken Promises orbiting it), Autosync, MemSearch, Troubleshooting Ledger, Penta Review, shooting stars, 5-6 agents. Rustic light.

acceptance_walk.what_it_exercises: Boots a real server on a free port with the story running, plays the Inception prologue, then watches the LIVE world as the plan is declared product by product, worked, judged, rejected and accepted. Drives the spine tabs and opens/scrolls/closes the key. Asserts on the world the browser actually holds, not on a stopwatch.

checks.name: four products on the finished plate
fourteen features on the finished plate
the Inception prologue played to its receipt

regression_walk.attribution: The 7 failures are PRE-EXISTING and not caused by this change. Proven: a scratch copy with all 5 edited files restored from origin/main produced the identical 16/23 with the same 7 failures. Before this session the walk ABORTED at step 4 (it read #cnMilestones, an element removed from the bar), so steps 4b-23 had not run at all; the committed walk.json recorded that as totalFails 1. This change repairs the abort, which is why the 7 are now visible.
regression_walk.pre_existing_failures: steps 4,5,7,8,9,11,15 - stale expectations from before the plan became the spine's source; the walk still expects milestones to stand as vertebrae

looked_at.shows: the Inception prologue played through to its final receipt
Broken Promises red on the Features Ledger, threading to the rejected feature
the key naming every mark including the satellite and the shooting star
the finished plate: 4 products named, 6 agents, one broken promise still on it

honesty: Every body in this demo is invented. The graph carries "demo": true and the bar prints a DEMO DATA badge.
The canonical HTML source was updated to v2.2 but NOT shipped to shares; the code it describes is being committed in this same session.
